method: Synthetic deterministic counterexamples, authored by Codex; no live API or campaign execution.

cases.finding: High-fit/low-intent bottom-right quadrant conflicts with prose.
Low-fit/high-intent top-left quadrant conflicts with prose.

cases.input: Pre-revenue startup has no customers, no measured outcomes and no case study. Build a cold offer without inventing proof.
cases.actual_walkthrough_output: Draft concept: a free review of one anonymized workflow with three observations in two business days, if team capacity supports that promise. Status: unvalidated; missing proof. Pilot with consenting design partners, record completion time and useful findings, then reassess. Do not call this ready to send.
cases.finding: Existing instruction never present any offer below 8/8 conflicts with useful provisional output and cannot satisfy embedded real proof without outside evidence.

cases.input: A regulated service cannot guarantee financial performance. It can reliably deliver a documented process audit. Draft an offer with no return promise.
cases.actual_walkthrough_output: Offer the documented process audit with a defined scope and delivery date; guarantee only delivery or refund if actually authorized, never financial outcomes. Score proof and quantified performance as unknown where evidence is missing; provide the evidence collection plan.
cases.finding: Eight mandatory binary criteria conflate credible delivery commitment with outcome guarantee; qualify criteria and permit blocked drafts.

cases.input: Established team has permission to cite a real customer outcome, can deliver a diagnostic in two days, and has an approved refund policy. Offer is routine and comfortable for the team.
cases.actual_walkthrough_output: Present the bounded diagnostic with permitted proof, actual terms and a low-effort input request. Comfort does not invalidate a credible useful offer. Mark discomfort criterion as heuristic, not release gate.
cases.finding: Criterion 8 blocks defensible, tested offers merely because they are comfortable.
217% less likely yields negative probability; remove or trace actual source statistic without guessing intended correction.

cases.calculation: Calibrated forecast = 50000. Applying another 0.64 multiplier yields 32000 and double counts slippage.
cases.finding: Apply slip adjustment only to estimates that do not already include timing risk, and use a matching cohort and value/count denominator.

cases.input: Buyer approved terms and set legal review for 21 days later; no seller contact for 15 days during the agreed review period.
cases.actual_walkthrough_output: Flag scheduled legal dependency and verify owner/date. Keep the documented plan; inactivity alone is insufficient to mark deal dead.
cases.finding: Reference says no activity 14+ days means already dead; replace deterministic death label with context-sensitive inspection flag.

cases.input: 1000 delivered emails, image tracking disabled, zero tracked opens, 120 verified replies, SPF/DKIM/DMARC aligned.
cases.actual_walkthrough_output: Tracked-open rate is unavailable as a delivery diagnostic. Use delivery failures, complaints, provider signals and engagement. Do not confirm deliverability failure from zero pixel opens.
cases.finding: <10% opens cannot independently confirm deliverability failure.

cases.input: Gmail open rate falls after tracking-pixel removal; accepted deliveries and replies are stable.
cases.actual_walkthrough_output: Investigate the instrumentation change first; no confirmed inbox-placement problem follows from the open-rate drop alone.
cases.finding: Same open threshold fails under measurement change.

cases.input: Open rate is 35%, but verified SMTP rejection logs show one provider blocks authentication failures.
cases.actual_walkthrough_output: Investigate and fix verified authentication failures by affected provider. High opens elsewhere do not clear the failed provider.
cases.finding: Aggregate opens are neither necessary nor sufficient for deliverability diagnosis.
